title: Foundation model
text:
### Frontier models

Certain highly advanced foundation models are termed "frontier models", whether because they expand the frontier (state of the art) or because they are considered above a certain threshold of risk.[1]

There is no single standard for assessing risks from frontier models. Some examples of dangerous capabilities include:

Designing and synthesizing new biological or chemical weapons[2]

Enabling novel offensive cyber attacks[3]

Evading human control through deceptive means[4]

It may be difficult to regulate the development and deployment of frontier models, due to limited interpretability,[5] unforeseen capability improvements, ease of misuse, and rapid proliferation.[5] If a frontier model is open-weight and publicly available online, the model can spread more rapidly, while the combination of greater customizability and non-revocable access exacerbates problems of accountability and regulatory oversight.[6]

Mitigating all harms that might arise from already-deployed frontier models becomes more difficult due to post-release modifications and attacks such as API fine-tuning[7] and prompt injection, as well as capabilities enhancements such as the agent harness, access to external resources (data, tools, systems), and orchestration among AI systems.[7]

The industry-led Frontier Model Forum was founded in July 2023 by OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, and Microsoft, with a stated goal of supporting safety research, best-practice standards, and information-sharing about advanced foundation models.[8] A network of national Artificial intelligence safety institutes (AISIs) have formed to assess risk from frontier models.[9]

### General-purpose AI

Foundation models adaptable to a wide range of use-cases are sometimes referred to as general-purpose AI. In designing the EU AI Act, the European Parliament has stated that a new wave of general-purpose AI technologies shapes the overall AI ecosystem.[10]

### World models

World models are sometimes described as foundation models.[11,12] World models are a representation of an environment intended to predict the state of that environment after taking a set of actions,[13,14] as well as to implicitly model physical concepts such as gravity.[14] Input prompts for world models can include text or images,[15,16] as well as videos or 3D scenes,[17] and the resulting 3D environments can be exported.[17] World models, alongside embodied AI, multi-agent models, and neuroscience models of the brain, are seen as alternatives to large language models for achieving general artificial intelligence.[18]

World models do not have a fully agreed definition, but have been divided into two scopes: one for representing and understanding the current environment, and another for predicting the future state of that environment. In the former view, world models are developed using model-based reinforcement learning and a Markov decision process, using model predictive control or Monte Carlo tree search to create policies. With the latter, (multimodal) large language models or video generation models can be used. In addition, these environments can be immersive simulations for training AI agents that can interact in the real world.[19]

### History

Quanta Magazine traced world models back to a 1943 publication by Kenneth Craik on mental models and the blocks world of SHRDLU in the 1960s.[20] Business Insider traced world models to a 1971 paper by Jay Wright Forrester.[18] A related idea of organizing world knowledge, the frame representation, was proposed by Marvin Minsky in 1974.[19]

In 2018, researchers David Ha and Jürgen Schmidhuber defined world models in the context of reinforcement learning: an agent with a variational autoencoder model V for representing visual observations, a recurrent neural network model M for representing memory, and a linear model C for making decisions. They suggested that agents trained on world models in environments that simulate reality could be applied to real world settings.[21]

In 2022, Yann LeCun saw a world model (defined by him as a neural network that acts as a mental model for aspects of the world that are seen as relevant) as part of a larger system of cognitive architecture – other neural networks that are analogous to different regions of the brain. In his view, this framework could lead to commonsense reasoning.[22,23] LeCun has estimated that world models would be fully functional by the late 2020s[24] to mid 2030s.[25]

### Training

World models are trained on a variety of data modalities, including text, images, audio and video, and have been applied to video generation.[26] One open source dataset for world models includes 1 billion data points across multiple modalities (text, images, audio, video and point clouds), including 1 million manual annotations.[14]

### Examples

TechCrunch saw Sora as an example of a world model,[26] while in January 2025, Nvidia released its own set of world models.[27,12] The South China Morning Post wrote that Manycore Tech was another example of companies aiming to build a world model, viewing their work as an example of spatial intelligence.[28] In May 2025, Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence released a world model for building simulations to test AI agents.[29]

Google DeepMind has also released two world models in two-dimensional space and three-dimensional space, respectively, that were trained on video data, with Google claiming that the latter can be a training environment for AI agents.[30,31] Meta released a world model in June 2025,[32] Tencent released an open source world model in July 2025.[33] Niantic, Inc. spinoff, Niantic Spatial, is developing a world model using anonymized player scans from Pokémon GO.[34,35] Other companies that are planning as of 2025 to build world models include ByteDance[33] and xAI.[36]

### Applications

Computer scientist researcher Fei-Fei Li views world models as applying to robotics and creative works. Due to the complexity of these models, she advocates for more complex strategies in data acquisition, data engineering, data processing, and synthesizing data.[37] She co-founded a startup on building world models, which, as of 2024, planned to do so in three phases: incorporating an understanding of three-dimensional space along with time; support for augmented reality; and support for robotics.[38] Her startup, World Labs, released its commercial world model, Marble, in November 2025.[39]

World models are intended for use in interactive media (such as video games and movies[40]) and environment simulation.[41] Proposed use cases for world models include action planning and outcome prediction.[39] Other applications include social simulacra to simulate social systems.[19] Wired compared world models to the metaverse,[38] while Business Insider noted possible military applications.[37]

In 2025, world models are being applied to drone warfare, robotics, and self-driving vehicles. The Wall Street Journal speculated that world models could improve spatial reasoning of artificial intelligence models and successfully automate both blue-collar and white-collar jobs.[42] As of October 2025, research has shown mixed results in the spatial reasoning capabilities of text-to-video models (in particular, Veo 3).[43]

In Ophthalmology, foundation models have been applied to retinal imaging including volumetric optical coherence tomography[44]

### Concerns

TechCrunch noted that world models could use more data than large language models and would require significantly more computational power (including the use of thousands of GPUs for training and inference).[23,26] It also noted the risk of hallucinations, coverage bias and algorithmic bias.[26] Similarly, The Financial Times noted the difficulty and expense in collecting data to simulate the world and training models to use that data.[36]

Creative professionals have expressed concern that world models could disrupt jobs in their industries.[41]

Other concerns include data privacy,[19] simulation of harmful situations,[19] misinformation and disinformation,[19] emergent behaviors,[45] and copyright.[40]
